column15: Owner corrected: Amahagan is the World Malt line of Nagahama Distillery (Nagahama Roman Beer Co, Shiga), NOT Hombo Shuzo/Mars - Amahagan is absent from Mars Whisky's own lineup page. Distillery uses both unpeated German and peated Scottish malt per jwhisky.com, peat varies by release; the World Malt Edition Peated SKU (search-level evidence only) is caught by the global peated keyword rule.

Core range (Classic, Double Maturation, Sherry Cask) unpeated per the producer's own site and retailers (non tourbe); two peated variants documented on the producer's own domain, covered by rules for Yeun Elez (50ppm Scottish peated malt) and Roch Du (lightly peated). defaultTypeName cleared: Warenghem also makes the WB blend (25% malt, 75% grain). Family-owned, led by David Roussier.

Colorado craft distillery (Vapor Distillery, ex-Roundhouse Spirits); range spans American single malt, bourbon and gin so defaultTypeName stays empty. Core range carries no peat language on the producer's own pages; the one Peated Malt SKU is a named exception the global peated keyword rule already catches. none is inferred from that naming split, not from an explicit unpeated statement.

Producer's own process page states the full grain bill (corn base plus rye, rye malt, barley malt) with no peat anywhere. Brand owned by Suntory Global Spirits since 2011; the Windsor plant itself passed to Pernod Ricard in 2005 and produces under contract.

column7: Grace O'Malley Spirits (Inis Tine Uisce Teoranta)
column15: No own distillery; sourced mainly from Great Northern Distillery, blended and finished at Good Spirits Bottling, Dundalk; majority stake held by Private Pier Industries (Berlin). Range spans blend, single malt (Stout Cask) and grain, so defaultTypeName stays empty. Peat corrected none to unknown: no statement found anywhere, and Irish whiskey has real peated exceptions, so absence of smoke notes is not a statement.

Identity resolved: Haran is the whisky brand of Destileria Manuel Acha (Amurrio, Alava, Basque Country, est. 1831, whisky since 1926) - not DYC and not the haran.es geology firm. Malt is kiln-dried with oak wood, not peat (leonandsonwine.com); whiskynotes.be on the 12yo: quite sure it is unpeated. An unverified Turba peated expression surfaced in search synthesis only - withheld, needs an opened source before a rule is added.

Park City, Utah producer blending own distillate with sourced stock (MGP, Barton); acquired by Constellation Brands in 2016. Bourbon and rye lines unpeated; the core Campfire product contains peated Scotch per the producer's own shop page, covered by a producer-scoped rule. kind could arguably be distillery (real working still) - left blend as seeded.

Brand owner's own product page: a slight hint of peat smoke is present but fleeting - light, on-domain corroboration. Owner confirmed from Campbell Meyer's own brand roster (East Kilbride; also McIvor and Bonnie & Clyde).

Ownership unresolved and conflicting: a distributor claims Loch Lomond production, but Loch Lomond Group's own brand list omits Highland Mist while listing comparable budget blends, and a US review attributes the US market to Sazerac/Barton Brands. Peat corrected none to unknown; withheld peat proposal: light per gspirits.eu tasting notes (3yo light peaty finish, Premium soft sweet smoky) - distributor copy, not producer domain.

Real blended Scotch presented by French bottler Fauconnier as its product (see the fauconnier row); a US trademark record title names Glen Turner Company Limited as owner but the page 403d twice, so owner stays empty. No smoke or peat language in either opened source; leans unpeated but kept unknown for lack of an explicit statement.

Owner confirmed as Ian Macleod Distillers via its own press release; the seed's Inver House suspicion is disconfirmed. Ordinary multi-region blend (Islands, Highlands, Lowlands, Speyside malt plus grain); official tasting language is sweet throughout and the 12yo charred woodsmoke reads as oak char, so none is kept under the ordinary-blend clause with brand-specific sources.

Same company as matsui (Matsui Shuzo, Kurayoshi Distillery, Tottori) - parentSlug set accordingly; a pure/vatted malt of sourced Scottish plus Japanese malt. No peat language for Kurayoshi products. Reviewer flag: the sibling Matsui line has a core The Peated expression on the producer's own site - check the matsui row's peat; that SKU name is caught by the global peated keyword rule.

English distillery (Bassenthwaite, Cumbria; founded 2012 by Paul Currie and Nigel Mills, not 2014; acquired by Nyetimber in June 2024). Core range uses unpeated Concerto barley (bbr.com) but the Whiskymaker's Reserve series is genuinely mixed - No.6 is described as heavily smoky in retail notes, No.5 and No.7 are not - so peat stays unknown at producer level. Withheld: the WR No.6 peat claim has no opened producer-domain source.

Islay single malt range from an undisclosed distillery, owned by Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers (independent, Brian and Jamie Morrison - NOT the Suntory-owned Morrison Bowmore). Islay sourcing confirmed on two producer-domain pages; core Terra and Mara land at 18-25ppm per converging retail sources, so medium. Flora Lightly Peated and the heavily peated Oloroso LE are handled by the global lightly/heavily peated keyword rules.

Morris of Rutherglen (Victoria); Casella Family Brands confirmed via the producer's own site footer. House style is fortified-wine-cask finishing with zero peat mentions on the official domain; the Smoked Muscat Barrel release's smoke is heavily-charred oak, not peat, per an independent review - kept unknown for lack of an explicit unpeated statement.

Non-distiller brand (HQ Rumson, New Jersey) producing at MGP's Ross & Squibb distillery; acquired by MGP through Luxco in 2023. Range spans straight bourbon AND straight rye plus finishes, so defaultTypeName cleared (was bourbon). American bourbon and rye mash bills use no peated malt.

New Zealand's largest single malt distillery (Waikato, founded 2017 by Matt and Celine Johns). The producer's own site never mentions peat; its smoky direction is manuka-wood smoked malt, not peat. whisky.com's database states Pokeno Origin is unpeated (seen via search results, page not opened - noted honestly). Peat upgraded unknown to none on that basis.

Ukraine-market private label owned by Ukrainian distributor Regno, contract-produced at an undisclosed large Tennessee distillery using the Lincoln County Process; the actual US distillery is unidentified. Range spans an Original and a Rye, so defaultTypeName cleared (was rye). No smoke language anywhere; American mash bills are unpeated. Probable Cyrillic spelling seen only in a retailer URL slug - not added as an alias.

Belfast-born (1830) brand relaunched by Halewood (HJ Neill Spirits); sources whiskey independent-bottler-style (Bushmills casks among sources) but products are own-branded, so kind stays blend. Range spans blend, single malt and single pot still, so defaultTypeName cleared. IE kept per the island-wide Irish Whiskey GI. none rests on category plus total absence of smoke language across the official range page and six reviews, not an explicit statement.

Blended Scotch range of London-based independent bottler Charles Edge (sister company Ethimex sources spirit); all four variants' own tasting notes carry no smoke language. Withheld peat proposal: light per IWSC judge notes on the 8yo (hints of bonfire smoke, a bit of Islay smoke) - competition notes, not producer statements.

Suntory's flagship single malt (Shimamoto, Osaka). Official pages describe the whole core range with zero smoke or peat language; whisky.com calls the malt usually unpeated (search-level). Peated spirit is distilled mainly for blending and appears only in clearly-labeled limited releases (2024 Kogei Peated Malt Spanish Oak), whose names the global peated keyword rule catches.

Kentucky straight bourbon brand produced at Limestone Branch Distillery (Lebanon, KY; Beam family and Luxco 50/50 since 2018; Luxco is MGP's branded-spirits division since 2021). Every current expression is straight bourbon, finishes included, so defaultTypeName is bourbon. The bourbon category uses no peated malt.

Italian private-label export brand for the Ukrainian market, manufactured by Polini (Bergamo, ~150 registered private labels) - attribution consistent across every Ukrainian retail listing, though Polini's own site does not showcase the brand. Base 3yo is a genuine blended whisky; Honey and Spicy variants are whisky-based flavored drinks, so defaultTypeName stays empty. Retailer copy conflicts on smoke (maudau says smoky-peaty, winestore floral-fruity), so peat stays unknown; withheld peat proposal: light per retailer copy only.
New row for yellowstone: the producing distillery (Lebanon, Kentucky; founded 2011 by Stephen and Paul Beam; Luxco took 50 percent in 2018). American bourbon house; no peated malt in the category.
